verification_scope: Local file hashes and native rule inventory only; this unsigned manifest does not authenticate authorship, grant license permission or establish detection accuracy.

license.note: No repository LICENSE or per-rule license declaration was present when this manifest was recorded. NOASSERTION is an unknown-license marker, not a license grant.

rules.name: crypto_miner
rules.limitations: Mining protocol/pool strings also occur in legitimate mining tools, documentation and examples; no malicious behavior is proven.

rules.name: crypto_miner_binary
rules.limitations: Miner names can appear in legitimate software or documentation; a name match does not establish execution or unauthorized mining.

rules.name: crypto_miner_config
rules.limitations: Generic configuration options can occur in benign command lines and documentation; two strings alone do not establish mining or malicious intent.

rules.name: eicar
rules.limitations: Test-only EICAR marker. A hit proves this test string was recognized, not that the file contains real malware.

rules.name: base64_url
rules.limitations: Encoded URLs also occur in benign data and examples; decoding context and destination reputation are not evaluated by this rule.

rules.name: network_iocs
rules.limitations: Any literal HTTP/HTTPS URL matches, including ordinary benign HTML and documentation. This is contextual evidence, not a malicious network verdict.

rules.name: suspicious_network_patterns
rules.limitations: Common download commands, user agents and TXT strings can appear in legitimate administration and documentation; two matches do not prove command-and-control.

rules.name: persistence_registry
rules.limitations: Registry paths can occur in legitimate startup configuration and documentation; a string match does not prove the registry was modified.

rules.name: suspicious_api_calls
rules.limitations: Windows memory/loading API names are common in benign development tools and documentation; two strings do not prove code injection.

rules.name: suspicious_dll_injection
rules.limitations: DLL-loading API and Windows library names are used by legitimate programs; their co-occurrence does not prove DLL injection.

rules.name: suspicious_process_injection
rules.limitations: Thread and mapping API names can occur in legitimate software and documentation; a string match does not prove process injection.

rules.name: asp_webshell
rules.limitations: Process, shell and filesystem strings are also used by legitimate administration code and documentation; this is a heuristic string match.

rules.name: generic_webshell
rules.limitations: Password/upload/permission strings are common in benign applications and examples; two strings do not establish a webshell.

rules.name: jsp_webshell
rules.limitations: ProcessBuilder( and getInputStream() are common benign Java APIs and also match this rule; a hit alone does not establish a webshell.

rules.name: php_webshell
rules.limitations: Patterns such as passthru(), shell_exec() and create_function() can occur in legitimate PHP utilities or examples; no taint flow or malicious intent is established.
